title: Duplicate Within Distance K
statement: Given an integer list nums and a non-negative integer k, return True if there exist two distinct indices i and j such that nums[i] == nums[j] and the positions are close, meaning abs(i - j) <= k; otherwise return False. Note that k is a distance bound, not a count, so a repeated value that sits more than k positions away does not count, and when k is 0 no pair of distinct indices can ever satisfy the bound. Return a plain boolean (True or False), never the pair of indices. If nums is empty or has a single element, return False.
hints: You only care about repeats that fall inside the last k positions as you scan left to right — what structure lets you ask 'is this value among the recent ones?' in O(1)?
Keep a set holding exactly the values of the trailing window of the previous k indices; before checking the current element, drop the value that has just slid out of range.

At index i, first evict nums[i - k - 1] (once i - k - 1 >= 0) so the set holds indices i-k..i-1, then return True if nums[i] is already in the set, otherwise add nums[i] and continue; return False if the scan ends.
